crossRefs.note: They deck it with silver and with gold. They fasten it with nails and with hammers, so that it can’t move.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came…
“ ‘ “Tarshish was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches. They traded for your wares with…
I lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, there was a man clothed in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold…
Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

people.name: Tarshish
people.line: Distant maritime city known for its wealth and trade

people.name: Uphaz
people.line: A place known for its fine gold

translations.web: There is silver beaten into plates, which is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the engraver and of the hands of the goldsmith. Their clothing is blue and purple. They are all the work of skillful men.
translations.bsb: Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz— the work of a craftsman from the hands of a goldsmith. Their clothes are blue and purple, all fashioned by skilled workers.
translations.kjv: Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning
translations.asv: There is silver beaten into plates, which is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the artificer and of the hands of the goldsmith; blue and purple for their clothing; they are all the work of skilful men.
